records.source: Πρεσβυτέρῳ μὴ ἐπιπλήξῃς, ἀλλὰ παρακάλει ὡς πατέρα, νεωτέρους ὡς ἀδελφούς, πρεσβυτέρας ὡς μητέρας, νεωτέρας ὡς ἀδελφὰς ἐν πάσῃ ἁγνείᾳ.
records.gloss: An older man not rebuke harshly, but appeal [to him] as a father, younger men as brothers, \v 2 older women as mothers, younger women as sisters, in all purity.
pieces: Never speak harshly to an older man, but appeal to him as you would to a father. Treat younger men as brothers,
older women as mothers, and younger women as sisters, with complete purity.

L.1: Do not rebuke an older man harshly, but appeal [to him] as [to] a father, to younger men as brothers,
L.2: to older women as mothers, to younger women as sisters, in all purity.

R.1: Do not speak angrily to an older man. Speak to him kindly, as if he were your father. Treat younger men like your brothers.
R.2: Treat older women like your mothers, and younger women like your sisters, with pure thoughts.

decisions.choice: an older man: an older man, not an elder in office
decisions.reason: Πρεσβυτέρῳ can mean an older man or an elder. Here it stands beside younger men, older women and younger women, so age is meant; elders in office come in verse 17.

decisions.choice: rebuke harshly ... appeal
decisions.reason: ἐπιπλήσσω is to strike at, rebuke sharply; παρακαλέω is to appeal to, urge, encourage.

decisions.choice: the church as a family
decisions.reason: Timothy is to treat each member as family: the church is God's household (3:15). "In all purity" goes especially with the younger women.

records.heading: Older and younger believers

records.source: Χήρας τίμα τὰς ὄντως χήρας.
records.gloss: Widows honor, the [ones] truly widows.
pieces: Give honor and support to widows who are really in need.

L.3: Honor widows who are truly widows.

R.3: Help and respect widows who have no one else to take care of them.

decisions.choice: honor: respect shown in practical support
decisions.reason: τιμάω is to honor, and here includes material support, as "honor" in verse 17 includes pay (verse 18; compare Matthew 15:4-6).

decisions.choice: truly widows: widows who have no family to support them
decisions.reason: Verse 5 explains: a true widow is left alone, with no one to care for her.

decisions.choice: give honor and support; really in need (B); have no one else to take care of them (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the honor involves and who the "true" widows are (m1, m2).

records.heading: Caring for widows

records.source: εἰ δέ τις χήρα τέκνα ἢ ἔκγονα ἔχει, μανθανέτωσαν πρῶτον τὸν ἴδιον οἶκον εὐσεβεῖν καὶ ἀμοιβὰς ἀποδιδόναι τοῖς προγόνοις, τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν ἀπόδεκτον ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: If but any widow children or grandchildren has, let them learn first [toward] their own household to show godliness and repayment to give back to the parents; this for is acceptable before the God.
pieces: But if a widow has children or grandchildren, they should first learn to put their faith into practice by caring for their own family, and so repay their parents and grandparents, for this pleases God.

L.4: But if any widow has children or grandchildren, let them first learn to show godliness toward their own household and to make some return to their parents, for this is pleasing before God.

R.4: But if a widow has children or grandchildren, they should learn that serving God means taking care of their own family. They should help their parents and grandparents, as they were helped. This pleases God.

decisions.choice: let them learn: the children and grandchildren
decisions.reason: μανθανέτωσαν is plural, and most naturally refers to the children and grandchildren: caring for a widowed mother or grandmother is their duty first.

decisions.choice: show godliness toward their own household, and repay their parents
decisions.reason: εὐσεβέω is to show reverence or devotion; caring for one's family is part of devotion to God (Exodus 20:12). προγόνοις means forebears, parents and grandparents.

decisions.choice: as they were helped
decisions.reason: Readable explains what "return" means.

records.source: ἡ δὲ ὄντως χήρα καὶ μεμονωμένη ἤλπικεν ἐπὶ θεὸν καὶ προσμένει ταῖς δεήσεσιν καὶ ταῖς προσευχαῖς νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας·
records.gloss: The but truly widow and left alone has hoped on God and continues in the requests and the prayers night and day;
pieces: The widow who is really in need, left all alone, has put her hope in God and keeps praying and asking for help night and day.

L.5: But the one who is truly a widow, left all alone, has set her hope on God and continues in supplications and prayers night and day.

R.5: A widow who is all alone trusts in God. Day and night she keeps praying and asking God for help.

decisions.choice: a widow who hopes in God and prays night and day: like Anna
decisions.reason: Anna the prophet, a widow, "worshiped night and day with fasting and prayer" (Luke 2:36-37). καὶ means left alone, with no family.

records.source: ἡ δὲ σπαταλῶσα ζῶσα τέθνηκεν.
records.gloss: The but living in luxury living is dead.
pieces: But the widow who lives for pleasure is dead even while she is alive.

L.6: But she who lives for pleasure is dead even while she lives.

R.6: But a widow who lives only for pleasure is dead in God's eyes, even though she is still alive.

decisions.choice: lives for pleasure: lives self-indulgently
decisions.reason: σπαταλάω is to live in luxury or self-indulgence (James 5:5).

decisions.choice: dead while living: spiritually dead
decisions.reason: Compare Revelation 3:1, "you have a name that you are alive, but you are dead".

decisions.choice: dead in God's eyes
decisions.reason: Readable says in what sense she is dead (m2).

records.source: καὶ ταῦτα παράγγελλε, ἵνα ἀνεπίλημπτοι ὦσιν·
records.gloss: And these things command, so that above reproach they may be;
pieces: Give these instructions as well, so that no one may be open to blame.

L.7: Command these things also, so that they may be above reproach.

R.7: Teach these things to the people, so that no one can say anything bad about them.

decisions.choice: they: the widows and their families
decisions.reason: ὦσιν is plural and probably takes in both the widows and the families who should care for them.

records.source: εἰ δέ τις τῶν ἰδίων καὶ μάλιστα οἰκείων οὐ προνοεῖ, τὴν πίστιν ἤρνηται καὶ ἔστιν ἀπίστου χείρων.
records.gloss: If but anyone his own and especially household members not provides for, the faith he has denied and is than an unbeliever worse.
pieces: Anyone who does not provide for their relatives, and especially for their own household, has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.

L.8: But if anyone does not provide for his own [relatives], and especially for [members of his] household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.

R.8: Anyone who does not take care of their relatives, and especially their own family, has turned away from the faith. They are worse than someone who does not believe.

decisions.choice: his own and especially his household: relatives, and above all those who live with him
decisions.reason: ἰδίων is one's own people; οἰκείων members of the same household.

decisions.choice: worse than an unbeliever: even unbelievers care for their families
decisions.reason: Caring for one's family was a duty everyone recognized; to neglect it is to fall below ordinary decency.

decisions.choice: anyone ... their
decisions.reason: The Greek "anyone" includes women; Balanced and Readable use "their". Literal keeps the Greek pronoun.

records.source: Χήρα καταλεγέσθω μὴ ἔλαττον ἐτῶν ἑξήκοντα γεγονυῖα, ἑνὸς ἀνδρὸς γυνή, ἐν ἔργοις καλοῖς μαρτυρουμένη, εἰ ἐτεκνοτρόφησεν, εἰ ἐξενοδόχησεν, εἰ ἁγίων πόδας ἔνιψεν, εἰ θλιβομένοις ἐπήρκεσεν, εἰ παντὶ ἔργῳ ἀγαθῷ ἐπηκολούθησεν.
records.gloss: A widow let be enrolled not less than of years sixty having been, of one man wife, \v 10 by works good being attested, if she brought up children, if she showed hospitality, if of holy ones feet she washed, if to those being afflicted she gave help, if every work good she followed.
pieces: No widow should be put on the list unless she is over sixty and has been faithful to her husband.
She must be well known for good deeds: bringing up children, welcoming strangers, washing the feet of God's people, helping those in trouble, and giving herself to every kind of good work.

L.9: Let a widow be enrolled if she is not less than sixty years old, [having been] the wife of one husband,
L.10: well attested for good works: if she has brought up children, if she has shown hospitality, if she has washed the feet of the holy ones, if she has helped the afflicted, if she has devoted herself to every good work.

R.9: A widow should be put on the church's list only if she is at least sixty years old. She must have been faithful to her husband.
R.10: People must know her for the good things she has done. Perhaps she raised children, welcomed guests into her home, washed the feet of God's people, helped people in trouble, or did all kinds of other good things.

decisions.choice: enrolled: put on the church's list of widows
decisions.reason: καταλέγω is to enter on a list. The church kept a list of widows it supported, who seem in turn to have given themselves to prayer and service (verse 5; Acts 6:1; 9:39-41).

decisions.choice: the wife of one husband: faithful to her husband
decisions.reason: The same form of words as in 3:2, "a one-man woman". It may mean married only once, which would match the advice in verse 14 that younger widows remarry only if it does not count against them, or faithful in marriage.

decisions.choice: washed the feet of the holy ones: humble hospitality
decisions.reason: Washing a guest's feet was a servant's task and a mark of welcome (John 13:14; Luke 7:44).

decisions.choice: faithful to her husband
decisions.reason: Balanced states one sense of m2, which is uncertain.

records.heading: The list of widows

records.source: νεωτέρας δὲ χήρας παραιτοῦ· ὅταν γὰρ καταστρηνιάσωσιν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, γαμεῖν θέλουσιν, ἔχουσαι κρίμα ὅτι τὴν πρώτην πίστιν ἠθέτησαν·
records.gloss: Younger but widows refuse; when for they feel sensual desires against the Christ, to marry they want, \v 12 having judgment because the first pledge they set aside;
pieces: But do not put younger widows on the list. When their desires pull them away from {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, they want to marry,
and so they come under judgment for breaking their first pledge.

L.11: But refuse [to enroll] younger widows, for when their desires draw them away from the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, they want to marry,
L.12: and so incur condemnation for having set aside their first pledge.

R.11: But do not put younger widows on the list. Their desire to marry again may become stronger than their wish to serve {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
R.12: Then they will be guilty of breaking the promise they made to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: their desires draw them away from Christ
decisions.reason: καταστρηνιάω is to feel strong (sensual) desire against something: desire to remarry draws them away from the service of Christ they had pledged.

decisions.choice: their first pledge: their promise to serve Christ as enrolled widows
alternatives: their first faith, their faith in Christ
decisions.reason: πίστιν usually means faith, but it can mean a pledge or promise. Here the context (enrollment, remarriage) points to a pledge the widows made when they were enrolled; it does not mean they abandoned Christian faith. Marriage itself is not condemned (verse 14).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article: "the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}".

decisions.choice: pledge (L, B); promise (R)
decisions.reason: The sense here is a pledge (m2), so the key term "faith" is not used.

records.source: ἅμα δὲ καὶ ἀργαὶ μανθάνουσιν, περιερχόμεναι τὰς οἰκίας, οὐ μόνον δὲ ἀργαὶ ἀλλὰ καὶ φλύαροι καὶ περίεργοι, λαλοῦσαι τὰ μὴ δέοντα.
records.gloss: At the same time and also idle they learn [to be], going around the houses, not only and idle but also gossips and busybodies, speaking the things not proper.
pieces: Besides, they get into the habit of being idle, going from house to house; and not only idle, but gossips and busybodies, talking about things they should not.

L.13: At the same time they also learn to be idle, going around from house to house, and not only idle but also gossips and busybodies, saying things they should not.

R.13: Also, they get used to having nothing to do and going from house to house. They gossip and get into other people's business, and they say things they should not say.

decisions.choice: gossips and busybodies
decisions.reason: φλύαροι is one who talks nonsense or gossips; περίεργοι one who meddles in others' affairs (compare 2 Thessalonians 3:11). "Things they should not" may include the false teaching (1:6; 2 Timothy 3:6-7).

records.source: βούλομαι οὖν νεωτέρας γαμεῖν, τεκνογονεῖν, οἰκοδεσποτεῖν, μηδεμίαν ἀφορμὴν διδόναι τῷ ἀντικειμένῳ λοιδορίας χάριν·
records.gloss: I want therefore younger [widows] to marry, to bear children, to manage the household, no occasion to give to the one opposing for reviling;
pieces: So I want the younger widows to marry, have children and manage their homes, giving the enemy no opportunity to speak evil of us.

L.14: So I want younger [widows] to marry, bear children, manage [their] households, and give the adversary no occasion for slander.

R.14: So I want younger widows to marry again, have children, and take care of their homes. Then our enemies will have no reason to say bad things about us.

decisions.choice: younger: younger widows
decisions.reason: νεωτέρας continues the subject of verse 11.

decisions.choice: the adversary: a human opponent, or Satan
decisions.reason: τῷ ἀντικειμένῳ may be any opponent of the church, or Satan (verse 15).

decisions.choice: [widows]
decisions.reason: The Greek has "younger [ones]"; the context gives widows (m1).

records.source: ἤδη γάρ τινες ἐξετράπησαν ὀπίσω τοῦ Σατανᾶ.
records.gloss: Already for some have turned aside after the Satan.
pieces: Some have already turned away to follow Satan.

L.15: For some have already turned aside to follow Satan.

R.15: Some widows have already turned away from Christ to follow Satan.

decisions.choice: some: some of the younger widows
decisions.reason: τινες probably refers to some of the younger widows, perhaps drawn in by the false teachers.

decisions.choice: Some widows have ... turned away from Christ
decisions.reason: Readable says who and from whom (m1).

records.source: εἴ τις πιστὴ ἔχει χήρας, ἐπαρκείτω αὐταῖς, καὶ μὴ βαρείσθω ἡ ἐκκλησία, ἵνα ταῖς ὄντως χήραις ἐπαρκέσῃ.
records.gloss: If any believing woman has widows, let her help them, and not let be burdened the church, so that the truly widows it may help.
pieces: If a believing woman has widows in her family, she should help them and not let the church be burdened, so that the church can help the widows who are really in need.

L.16: If any believing woman has widows [in her family], let her help them, and let the church not be burdened, so that it may help those who are truly widows.

R.16: If a woman who believes has widows in her family, she should help them. Then the church will not have to care for them, and it can help the widows who have no one else.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "any believing woman"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "any believing man or woman". The shorter reading may refer to a woman of means who had widows in her household.

records.source: Οἱ καλῶς προεστῶτες πρεσβύτεροι διπλῆς τιμῆς ἀξιούσθωσαν, μάλιστα οἱ κοπιῶντες ἐν λόγῳ καὶ διδασκαλίᾳ·
records.gloss: The well leading elders of double honor let be considered worthy, especially those laboring in word and teaching;
pieces: Elders who lead the church well should be thought worthy of double honor, especially those who work hard at preaching and teaching.

L.17: Let the elders who lead well be considered worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in preaching and teaching.

R.17: Elders who lead the church well should be respected and paid well, especially those who work hard at preaching and teaching.

decisions.choice: elders: the church's leaders
decisions.reason: πρεσβύτεροι here means the leaders of the church, the same people called overseers in 3:1-7 (Titus 1:5-7).

decisions.choice: double honor: respect and payment
alternatives: twice the support given to widows
honor both as older men and as leaders
decisions.reason: τιμῆς means honor, and verse 18 shows that it includes pay. "Double" may mean generous, or both respect and support.

decisions.choice: respected and paid well
decisions.reason: Readable states the sense of m2.

records.heading: Instructions about elders

records.source: λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφή· Βοῦν ἀλοῶντα οὐ φιμώσεις, καί· Ἄξιος ὁ ἐργάτης τοῦ μισθοῦ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Says for the Scripture: An ox threshing not you shall muzzle, and: Worthy [is] the worker of the wages of him.
pieces: For the Scripture says, "Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain," and "The worker deserves to be paid."

L.18: For the Scripture says, "You shall not muzzle an ox while it is threshing," and, "The worker [is] worthy of his wages."

R.18: The Scripture says, "Do not cover the mouth of an ox while it is working to separate the grain," and "Workers should be paid for their work."

decisions.choice: do not muzzle an ox: Deuteronomy 25:4
decisions.reason: An ox treading grain was allowed to eat as it worked (Deuteronomy 25:4). Paul draws the same lesson in 1 Corinthians 9:9-10.

decisions.choice: the worker deserves his wages: the words of Jesus
decisions.reason: These are Jesus' words in Luke 10:7 (compare Matthew 10:10). Both sayings are introduced together as "the Scripture says".

decisions.choice: threshing: oxen walked over grain to separate it from the husk
decisions.reason: ἀλοάω is to thresh by having animals tread the grain on a threshing floor.

decisions.choice: while it is working to separate the grain
decisions.reason: Readable explains threshing (m3).

records.source: κατὰ πρεσβυτέρου κατηγορίαν μὴ παραδέχου, ἐκτὸς εἰ μὴ ἐπὶ δύο ἢ τριῶν μαρτύρων·
records.gloss: Against an elder an accusation not receive, except unless on two or three witnesses;
pieces: Do not listen to an accusation against an elder unless it is supported by two or three witnesses.

L.19: Do not accept an accusation against an elder except on [the evidence of] two or three witnesses.

R.19: Do not believe someone who accuses an elder of doing wrong, unless two or three people say it is true.

decisions.choice: two or three witnesses: Deuteronomy 19:15
decisions.reason: The law required two or three witnesses for any charge (Deuteronomy 19:15; Matthew 18:16; 2 Corinthians 13:1). Leaders are protected from unfounded accusations.

records.source: τοὺς ἁμαρτάνοντας ἐνώπιον πάντων ἔλεγχε, ἵνα καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ φόβον ἔχωσιν.
records.gloss: Those sinning before all rebuke, so that also the rest fear may have.
pieces: Those who keep on sinning should be rebuked in front of everyone, so that the others will also take warning.

L.20: Rebuke those who sin in front of everyone, so that the rest also may be afraid.

R.20: If elders keep on sinning, correct them in front of the whole church. Then the others will be afraid to do wrong.

decisions.choice: those who sin: elders who persist in sin
decisions.reason: The present ἁμαρτάνοντας suggests continuing in sin; in context it refers to elders proved guilty (verse 19).

records.source: διαμαρτύρομαι ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν ἀγγέλων, ἵνα ταῦτα φυλάξῃς χωρὶς προκρίματος, μηδὲν ποιῶν κατὰ πρόσκλισιν.
records.gloss: I solemnly charge before the God and Christ Jesus and the elect angels, that these things you keep without prejudice, nothing doing by partiality.
pieces: In the presence of God and {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus and the chosen angels, I solemnly charge you to keep these instructions without prejudging anyone and to do nothing out of favoritism.

L.21: I solemnly charge [you] before God and {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus and the chosen angels to keep these [instructions] without prejudice, doing nothing out of partiality.

R.21: God, {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus and the angels God has chosen are watching. In their presence I give you this serious command: obey these instructions without deciding anything ahead of time, and do not favor anyone.

decisions.choice: the chosen angels: the angels who serve God
decisions.reason: Angels were thought of as witnesses of what God's people do (1 Corinthians 4:9; Luke 9:26). "Chosen" sets them apart from fallen angels.

decisions.choice: without prejudice, without partiality
decisions.reason: προκρίματος is a judgment made beforehand; πρόσκλισιν leaning toward one side.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

records.source: χεῖρας ταχέως μηδενὶ ἐπιτίθει, μηδὲ κοινώνει ἁμαρτίαις ἀλλοτρίαις· σεαυτὸν ἁγνὸν τήρει.
records.gloss: Hands quickly on no one lay, nor share in sins of others; yourself pure keep.
pieces: Do not be in a hurry to lay hands on anyone, and do not share in other people's sins. Keep yourself pure.

L.22: Do not lay hands on anyone hastily, and do not share in the sins of others; keep yourself pure.

R.22: Do not be too quick to put your hands on anyone to make them a church leader. If you do, you will share the blame for their sins. Keep yourself pure.

decisions.choice: laying on hands: setting someone apart for leadership
alternatives: restoring a repentant sinner to the church
decisions.reason: In this letter the laying on of hands commissions people for service (4:14). In context, Timothy should not appoint elders hastily, or he will share the blame if they fall into sin (verses 19-20). Some take it of receiving back those who had been disciplined.

decisions.choice: to make them a church leader
decisions.reason: Readable states the sense chosen in m1.

records.source: μηκέτι ὑδροπότει, ἀλλὰ οἴνῳ ὀλίγῳ χρῶ διὰ τὸν στόμαχον καὶ τὰς πυκνάς σου ἀσθενείας.
records.gloss: No longer drink only water, but wine a little use because of the stomach and the frequent of you illnesses.
pieces: Stop drinking only water, and take a little wine for your stomach and your frequent illnesses.

L.23: No longer drink only water, but use a little wine for the sake of your stomach and your frequent illnesses.

R.23: Do not drink only water. Drink a little wine to help your stomach, because you are often sick.

decisions.choice: a little wine for your stomach: wine as medicine
decisions.reason: Water was often unsafe, and wine was used as medicine (Luke 10:34). Timothy may have avoided wine to keep clear of the drinking condemned in 3:3, 3:8; Paul's advice keeps "pure" (verse 22) from being taken as harsh treatment of the body (4:3).

records.source: Τινῶν ἀνθρώπων αἱ ἁμαρτίαι πρόδηλοί εἰσιν, προάγουσαι εἰς κρίσιν, τισὶν δὲ καὶ ἐπακολουθοῦσιν·
records.gloss: Of some men the sins evident are, going before into judgment, some but also they follow;
pieces: Some people's sins are obvious, going ahead of them to judgment; the sins of others show up later.

L.24: The sins of some people are evident, going before [them] to judgment, but [the sins] of others follow after.

R.24: Some people's sins are easy to see, even before they are judged. But other people's sins are seen only later.

decisions.choice: some sins are plain beforehand, some come to light later
decisions.reason: The saying explains verse 22: take time before appointing anyone, because not every fault is visible at once.

records.source: ὡσαύτως καὶ τὰ ἔργα τὰ καλὰ πρόδηλα, καὶ τὰ ἄλλως ἔχοντα κρυβῆναι οὐ δύνανται.
records.gloss: Likewise also the works the good evident [are], and those otherwise being to be hidden not are able.
pieces: In the same way, good deeds are obvious, and even those that are not cannot stay hidden.

L.25: Likewise also good works are evident, and even those that are not cannot be hidden.

R.25: In the same way, some good things people do are easy to see. And even the good things that are not easy to see will not stay hidden forever.

decisions.choice: those that are otherwise: good works not yet seen
decisions.reason: τὰ ἄλλως ἔχοντα most likely means good works that are not obvious; they too will come to light.
